02What is digital marketing?

Component of marketing that uses internet and online digital technologies (desktop, mobile, other platforms) to promote products and services — strategies to reach customers and convince them toward purchase.

Channels

  • Social media
  • Content marketing
  • Website marketing
  • SEO and more

03Benefits of digital marketing

Know our audience +
Better targeting → less wasted spend on people who will never buy.
Doesn't cost much +
Startups can compete with big brands on small budgets.
Anyone, anywhere +
Sell beyond physical location — reach customers online globally.
Adaptable +
Change creative overnight; pause or tweak campaigns in minutes.
Personalize by channel +
Right message on FB vs email vs search for the same product.
In the real world — Kathmandu café Click
A Kathmandu café can run a Facebook page ad to nearby phones for a few hundred rupees — same night — while a billboard would take weeks and cost far more. (Teaching example)

04Channels in practice

Same toolkit, different surfaces — social, search, marketplaces, and wallets.

🛒

Marketplace

💳

📱

Social pages

05Online advertisement

Marketing using the Internet to deliver promotional messages. When software does the purchasing = programmatic advertising.

  • Includes email, SEM, social media, display, mobile
  • Publisher integrates ads; advertiser provides ads
  • Gross revenue of online ads rising vs declining traditional
Advertiser → Ad / network → Publisher site

06Ad targeting

Marketers place ads in specific areas on specific platforms to increase visibility and engagement with a target audience.

  • Look and placement determined by audience behaviours and interests
  • Strategically placed for a clearly defined audience based on past customer behaviour and other data
  • Consumers want personalized messages
  • Relevant ads on platforms they visit increase interest
Why does targeting matter? Click to reveal
Without targeting you pay to show ads to people who will never buy. Behaviour + interest data steers spend toward higher-intent users — the same idea behind retargeting someone who abandoned a cart.

07Search Engine Marketing (SEM)

Use of search engines to build and sustain brands. Search engine advertising supports direct sales to online consumers.

~2%
Average CTR for search engine advertising — fairly steady
>90%
Google share — top search engine in Western Europe
Search engines derive most revenue from banner advertisements.

08Two types of search ads

1. Pay-Per-Click (PPC)

Keyword advertising — the primary type. Merchants purchase keywords via bidding; when a consumer searches that word, the ad shows (small text on right, or listing at top).

Rank More paid → higher visibility. Some engines also rank by popularity — rank depends on amount paid and clicks per unit time.

2. Network keyword (AdSense)

Context advertising — Google AdSense (2002). Publishers join networks; the search engine places relevant ads on their sites.

Revenue split Advertisers pay; revenue split between search engine and publisher — publisher often gets more than half.
In the real world — PPC example Click
Google Ads for “best laptop Kathmandu” — the sponsored listing sits above organic results; you pay when someone clicks, not when they merely see the ad. (Teaching example)
Quick check
In PPC keyword ads, when does the advertiser typically pay?
Correct: Pay-per-click means you pay for the click. Impressions alone usually do not charge in classic PPC (though other models like CPM exist for display).

09Search Engine Optimization (SEO)

Improving ranking of pages with search engines by altering content and design of web pages and site.

  • Carefully select keywords, update content frequently
  • Design so search engine programs can easily read the site → better impact and ROI
  • Google and others frequently change algorithms
  • Semantic search: attempting to capture more of what the user intended or might like to know
Organic vs paid — teaching example Click
A blog post titled “How to choose a trekking bag in Nepal” can rank for that long-tail query without paying per click — organic traffic vs paid SEM.

10Display ad marketing — types 1–4

Digital marketing delivering video/content via interactive media such as websites.

1. Banner ads

Oldest and most popular; least effective and lowest cost. Rectangular box on desktop or mobile.

2. Rich media

Animation, sound, interactivity (HTML5, JS) — far more effective than simple banners.

3. Interstitial

“In between” — full-page ad as the user moves from one page to the next.

4. Video ads

TV-like ads as in-page video before, during, or after content.

11Display ads — types 5–9

5. Sponsorship +
Paid tie of advertiser's name to info, event, or venue — branding over immediate sales.
6. Native ads +
Don't look like ads; similar to editorial content on the host site.
7. Content marketing +
Brand content campaign — visitors, organic rankings, social engagement.
8. Ad networks +
Sell ad opportunities; sites act as web publishers in the network.
9. Exchanges / RTB +
Programmatic + real-time bidding — automated auction matching supply & demand of page space.
In the real world Click
YouTube pre-roll · Daraz homepage banners · native: sponsored articles that look like news. (Teaching examples)

12E-mail marketing

Sending commercial messages typically to a group using email — builds loyalty, trust, or brand awareness.

Transactional emails +
Triggered by a customer action; convey information about that action (e.g. order confirmation).
Direct emails +
Promotional message to a collected customer list (e.g. flash-sale blast).
Quick distinction Click
Order confirmation after buying shoes = transactional. “Flash sale tonight — 20% off” to your subscriber list = direct (promotional). (Teaching example)

13Affiliate marketing

Firm pays commission (typically 4%–20%) to other websites (including blogs) for sending customers.

  • Pay-for-performance — paid only if users click or purchase
  • ~10% of online retail sales via affiliate programs
  • Amazon: strong program, 1M+ associates, up to 10% advertising fees on referral sales
4–20%
Typical commission range
~10%
Online retail via affiliates
1M+
Amazon Associates

14Affiliate — how value flows

Merchant → Affiliate link → Blog / site → Reader clicks → Purchase → commission
In the real world Amazon Associates: a blogger reviews a camera, adds an affiliate link; when readers buy, the blogger earns a commission — pay only for results.
Exam tip: what makes affiliate “performance”? Click
Unlike a fixed sponsorship fee, the merchant pays only if users click or purchase — classic pay-for-performance.

15Mobile & local — the visual

Two of the three major e-commerce marketing trends (with social). Mobile devices accelerated local search and buying.

16Mobile marketing

Display banners, rich media, video, games, email, SMS, QR codes. Now a required part of the standard marketing budget.

17Local marketing

Third major trend in e-commerce marketing (with social and mobile). Mobile devices accelerated local search and purchasing.

Quick check
Which metric measures the % of visitors who become customers?
Correct: Conversion rate = % of visitors who become customers (visitor → buyer). CTR is % of ads clicked; stickiness is time on site.

18Online marketing metrics

Traditional display / email

  • Impressions — times an ad is served
  • CTR — % of times ad is clicked
  • VTR — visit within 30 days (not immediate click)
  • Viewability · Reach · Stickiness
  • Conversion rate — % visitors → customers
From the notes Click
Search ads often see CTR around ~2%. Conversion = visitor → buyer — the metric that ties traffic to revenue.

19Video & email metrics

Video advertising

  • View time
  • Completion rate
  • Skip rate

Email metrics

  • Open rate
  • Delivery rate
  • Click-through rate
  • Bounce-back rate
  • Unsubscribe rate
  • Conversion rate
Why track skip rate on video? Click
High skip rate means the first seconds failed to hook viewers — fix creative or targeting before burning more budget.

20Pricing models — 1–4

1. Pricing +
Putting value on a product and service.
2. Law of one price +
With complete price transparency — one world price for every product.
3. Demand curve +
Quantity of goods that can be sold at various prices.
4. Price discrimination +
Selling to different groups based on willingness to pay.

21Pricing models — 5–8

5. Free & freemium +
Basic free; pay to upgrade to premium.
6. Versioning +
Multiple versions of information goods — same product, different segments, different prices.
7. Bundling +
Two or more goods for a reduced price.
8. Dynamic pricing +
Price varies with demand of customer and supply situation of seller.
In the real world Click
Spotify freemium · Netflix tiers (versioning) · ecommerce bundle deals (phone + case). (Teaching examples)
Quick check
“Basic free; pay to upgrade” describes which pricing idea?
Correct: Freemium = free basic tier + paid premium upgrade (e.g. Spotify). Bundling is multiple goods at a reduced price.

27Key takeaways

Digital = reach + convert +
Internet/digital platforms — low cost, adaptable, personalizable. Example: same café promo on FB vs billboard.
SEM vs SEO +
SEM: PPC bid keywords vs AdSense context ads. SEO: organic rank; semantic search aims at intent.
Display · email · affiliate +
Banners → RTB; transactional vs direct email; affiliate commissions often ~4–20%.
Mobile & local +
Required trends — geotargeting, apps, daily deals matter for nearby buyers.
Metrics & pricing +
Know CTR, VTR, conversion… and freemium, versioning, bundling, dynamic pricing.
Platform toolkits +
FB free+paid/FBX · Twitter promoted · Pinterest Rich/Promoted Pins · AdSense for publishers.
